gcp_vertex.name: GCP Agent Sandbox
gcp_vertex.customization_summary: Tested integration: agent-sandbox run with the default Google-managed Python code sandbox under an Agent Engine/Agent Runtime parent. No CPU, RAM, image, GPU or network settings are sent by the adapter. Current official BYOC templates offer image, CPU/memory requests and limits, ports and internet_access, but that separate managed-container path was not tested. GKE Agent Sandbox and Compute Engine GPU VMs are infrastructure alternatives, not capabilities measured for this adapter.

custom_image.notes: Official BYOC uses an Artifact Registry image and a custom-container sandbox template. The tested default code sandbox has no image selector; local shell/CMEK references explicitly lack end-to-end verification.

runtime_packages.notes: The report verifies installing one uploaded pure-Python fixture wheel via pip --no-index --no-deps --target, then importing it. This is not online package installation or arbitrary native dependencies. Official code-sandbox docs say own libraries cannot be installed; retain this narrow observed exception rather than generalizing it. BYOC is the documented dependency-customization path.

cpu_sizing.notes: BYOC templates document CPU requests/limits. The tested adapter requests none; its cost estimate assumes 2 vCPU, not an allocation attestation. A separate 2026-10-01 local probe saw 8 visible CPUs and roughly 2x CPU parallel speedup, neither a contractual allocation nor current-run inventory.

memory_sizing.notes: BYOC templates document memory requests/limits. The tested adapter requests none; 4 GB in report cost metadata is an estimate. The separate 2026-10-01 reference measured 2 GiB, illustrating why actual current allocation remains unknown.

gpu.notes: No GPU requested/tested. Current guest inventory reports nvidia-smi unavailable, which does not establish platform-wide GPU eligibility. Reviewed BYOC example does not establish accelerator support. Compute Engine and compatible GKE GPU deployments are separate choices.

network_policy.notes: The official code sandbox has no network access; the local probe concurs, contradicting has_internet_access=true in the adapter. BYOC documents egress_control_config.internet_access. The tested adapter sends no network policy and the evaluation campaign does not attest effective policy.

persistent_storage.notes: Files/state survive calls within a live sandbox, not deletion. Current lifecycle docs describe filesystem-preserving pause/resume, but code-sandbox snapshots are explicitly unsupported and the adapter uses one-shot deletion. Durable cross-deletion storage and pause/resume were not tested.

session_reuse.notes: Code execution can reuse state by sandbox ID. Local start/exec supports this, but this adapter calls run for every execution and does not retain a remote session. Current docs advertise up to 14 days; the bundled CLI caps TTL at 3600s and the adapter caps its requested TTL at 900s.

shell.notes: The offline-wheel workload executes a pip subprocess inside the code sandbox. Local tooling also documents bash via the code sandbox. This does not attest a separately provisioned shell-container sandbox under CMEK.

file_transfer.notes: The evaluation verifies a 26900-byte artifact round trip by expected size and SHA-256 and verifies summary.json. The adapter passes --upload and reads output files. Official request/response limit is 100 MB in aggregate; unlimited stdout rendering is not unlimited API payload size.

ports_preview.notes: BYOC templates document ports. That is not evidence of an automatically public preview URL. The tested code adapter has no port exposure or preview integration.

self_hosting.notes: This service is Google-managed. A locally running client does not self-host its sandbox. Kubernetes-SIGs/GKE Agent Sandbox and Compute Engine VMs are separate infrastructure deployments.

cmek.notes: CMEK is configured at parent runtime creation and inherited by sandboxes/templates/snapshots for at-rest content, not resource metadata. modal.name: Modal
modal.customization_summary: Managed Sandbox API with custom built/registry images, fractional physical CPU requests and limits, memory requests and limits in MiB, optional GPUs on gVisor, network controls, volumes and snapshots. The inspected adapter requests debian_slim, 2 physical cores and 2048 MiB, not a hard 2-vCPU/4-GB machine; observed reports do not inventory the allocation.

custom_image.notes: Sandbox.create accepts modal.Image; method-chained, external registry and published named images are documented. Cached external tags are treated as immutable after pull; pin versions for reproducibility. Adapter uses Image.debian_slim without a pinned Python version or image digest.

runtime_packages.notes: Arbitrary exec supports runtime package installation subject to permissions and egress. Existing dependency_install evaluations pass an uploaded offline wheel installed with --no-index/--no-deps into a private target; this does not measure PyPI availability or system-package installation.

cpu_sizing.notes: cpu is fractional physical cores (1 physical core = 2 vCPU equivalent); a scalar is a request, (request, limit) adds throttling. Default request is 0.125 physical cores. Current docs enforce a scheduling maximum without publishing its number on the cited pages. Adapter cpu=2 is a request for 2 physical cores, not 2 vCPUs; allocation/burst usage is not measured.

memory_sizing.notes: memory uses MiB; a scalar is a guaranteed request, (request, limit) adds a hard OOM ceiling. Default is 128 MiB. Adapter memory=2048 requests 2 GiB and supplies no hard limit. Report cost.details.ram_gb=4 is an unverified estimator input, not measured RAM.

gpu.notes: Explicit Sandbox GPU reservation exists; GPU sandboxes require runtime=gvisor and are subject to preemption. GPU Function/model-hosting support is not the evidence used here. Adapter requests no GPU; GPU access and availability were not benchmarked.

network_policy.notes: Public outbound IP access by default; block_network, outbound CIDR allowlists, beta domain allowlists and inbound CIDR allowlists are available. Domain filtering uses TLS SNI on 443, does not inspect Host/path, permits unrestricted DNS unless fully blocked, and has domain-fronting limitations. Dynamic updates are experimental and require allowlist types at creation. Adapter sets none of these controls.

persistent_storage.notes: Mount named Volumes/NetworkFileSystems or snapshot filesystem/directory state for later Sandboxes. Root filesystem persistence during an active sandbox is distinct from storage surviving termination. Adapter mounts no durable storage and terminates on cleanup. Sandbox disk cannot be enlarged; VM root disk is fixed at 512 GiB.

session_reuse.notes: from_id/from_name can reconnect to running sandboxes. Current adapter retains its handle across calls; existing session_state evaluations pass three filesystem-state API calls. Each exec starts a new process, so Python globals are not the measured continuity. Documented lifetime defaults to 300 seconds, maximum 24 hours; adapter uses 180 seconds and terminates at cleanup.

shell.notes: Sandbox.exec supports arbitrary command argv and PTYs. Adapter selects python -c for Python and bash -c otherwise. Existing evaluated workloads primarily exercise Python and its subprocesses, not a separately evaluated shell-language request.

file_transfer.notes: Native filesystem write_bytes/read_bytes and local copy APIs are documented. Adapter stages input bytes and lists output directory entries; existing artifact_roundtrip reports pass byte/hash validation for a 26900-byte artifact. Nested-directory export and large-file API limits are not established by that result.

ports_preview.notes: Authenticated HTTP/WebSocket connect tokens and explicit TLS/plain TCP or HTTP/2 tunnels exist. Default sandbox has no public inbound listener. Tunnel custom domains require Team/Enterprise and manual onboarding. Adapter does not expose ports or generate previews.

self_hosting.notes: Inspected official Sandbox/security docs describe Modal-operated compute. No full customer-operated Sandbox control/data-plane distribution was verified. An open-source client, runtime=vm or underlying cloud selection does not establish self-hosting.

cmek.notes: Provider-managed encryption at rest is documented. Alpha customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK) are explicitly supported for directory snapshots only; customer passes raw key material on create/mount and Modal does not persist it. This is not verified KMS-backed CMEK for the whole sandbox, volumes, images or logs. Adapter configures neither CSEK nor CMEK.

blaxel.name: Blaxel
blaxel.customization_summary: Managed sandbox microVMs with custom images containing sandbox-api, memory-sized CPU, network/proxy options, volumes and previews. CPU is coupled to RAM. Current adapter requests a unique per-attempt name, py-app:latest, 4096 MB, us-pdx-1 and ttl=1h; options allow alternate image/memory/region/TTL. Exact requested settings and guest observations are recorded in tested-configurations.json. No GPU deployment tested.

custom_image.notes: Dockerfile/custom registry images must include sandbox-api; SDK ImageInstance injects the binary/default entrypoint. Generic unmodified Docker Hub images cannot directly act as sandbox images. Default slimming removes build-time compilers/caches; opt out where runtime builds need them. Adapter requests a mutable prebuilt py-app:latest tag.

runtime_packages.notes: Official sandbox use cases describe autonomous package installation and process execution. Availability depends on image tools, writable RAM-backed filesystem and egress policy. Legacy package_ecosystem report establishes pip availability, not a verified package installation; no new evaluated installation report was available.

cpu_sizing.notes: CPU follows selected memory, not an independent CPU field in inspected SandboxRuntime. API description says memory MB/2048 (4096 MB=2 CPUs), while overview examples say 8 GB=4 cores and 16 GB=6 cores. Do not extrapolate a universal linear mapping or assign physical/vCPU equivalence without inventory. Adapter requests 4096 MB; actual existing-instance CPU is unknown.

memory_sizing.notes: memory is documented in MB; limits depend on account tier, custom pricing advertises up to 256 GB. Image base is read-only EROFS with writable tmpfs layer sharing RAM, approximately 50% reserved when possible. memory=4096 is a requested creation value, not measured process-available RAM; create_if_not_exists does not reconfigure existing instances.

gpu.notes: No GPU reservation field in the inspected sandbox API/runtime configuration or explicit managed Sandbox GPU offering verified. Agent Hosting, model integrations, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES image examples, NVIDIA-branded tools and custom hardware marketing do not prove sandbox GPU access. No GPU requested or tested. Absence of documentation is not an explicit unsupported contract.

network_policy.notes: Public-preview proxy domain/method/path filters; environment-variable routing alone can be bypassed. Explicit firewall rulesets=[proxy] at creation enforces proxy egress, documented for Mark 3.0 not Carbon/3.1. API relocates allow/deny fields under network.proxy and has conflicting rule-precedence wording versus guide; verify exact version semantics before relying on overlap. Adapter configures no network restriction.

persistent_storage.notes: Standby snapshots retain state; attached Volumes survive deletion. Current guide limits one volume per sandbox, same region, create-time attach. Adapter mounts no durable storage and deletes its owned sandbox during cleanup/teardown with errors propagated.

session_reuse.notes: Named lookup/reuse and standby restore are documented. Adapter now uses a unique per-attempt sandbox and does not declare reusable session calls. Legacy single-script multi-turn is not separate-call or standby/resume evidence.

shell.notes: process.exec accepts arbitrary shell command strings; named process wait/kill supported. Adapter always runs an uploaded Python script and combines logs. Without keepAlive, documented timeout bounds waiting and does not auto-kill process; adapter reports timed_out on wait timeout but does not call process.kill.

file_transfer.notes: Provider supports native binary read/write and multipart transfer (direct HTTP request cap 5 MB, SDK chunks larger writes). Current adapter instead UTF-8-decodes inputs with errors=ignore, text-writes, and text-reads only /tmp/transformed_output.txt. Legacy 6000-byte text roundtrip does not validate arbitrary binary or multi-file fidelity.

ports_preview.notes: Creation-time API ports and dynamic public/private token previews; preview URLs can use custom domains. API reserves 80/443/8080; preview guide explicitly forbids port 80. Bind to injected HOST; active WebSocket connections have timeout/reconnect constraints. Adapter exposes no ports/previews.

self_hosting.notes: Pricing describes bring-your-own-metal: customer bare metal in own VPC connected privately to Blaxel control plane, with quote/custom hardware. This is partial infrastructure control, not a verified wholly self-operated control plane/runtime distribution. Evaluated path remains managed cloud.

cmek.notes: No provider-native customer KMS encryption-key binding/rotation/revocation contract for sandbox snapshots, volumes, images or logs verified in inspected sources. BYOM, encrypted secrets or ZDR assertions do not establish CMEK. Adapter declares cmek_supported=False without an encryption test.

runtime_packages.notes: Existing dependency_install evaluations pass installation/import of an uploaded offline wheel in a private directory using --no-index/--no-deps. This tests runtime Python package installation, not internet package registry connectivity or apt/sudo privileges.

gpu.notes: Official GPU FAQ explicitly states sandboxes are CPU-only with no GPU SDK/CLI/API/template option; BYOC does not change this. Calling remote inference, installing CUDA libraries, or running an agent that orchestrates GPU training elsewhere is not local sandbox GPU access.

network_policy.notes: Default public egress; allow_internet_access switch, IP/CIDR allow/deny rules, HTTP 80 Host and TLS 443 SNI domain allowlisting. Allow rules override denies; domain mode requires deny-all and allows default DNS server. Domain filtering does not cover QUIC/other ports and shared endpoints have limitations. Runtime update_network replaces rules. Adapter uses defaults and tests no custom policy.

persistent_storage.notes: Pause/resume preserves filesystem and memory; paused retention is indefinite until explicit kill. Adapter kills at cleanup and mounts no volume; measured session state is not persistence after kill.

session_reuse.notes: Connect to a running/paused sandbox; adapter retains one Code Interpreter sandbox across calls and session_state evaluation passes three separate filesystem calls. shell.notes: Provider commands.run supports foreground/background shell commands. Adapter instead submits all code to run_code with no language selector, so generic shell capability is not a native shell-request route in this integration.

file_transfer.notes: files.write/read APIs; adapter transfers input bytes, reads output with format=bytes and hashes it. ports_preview.notes: get_host(port) generates a public HTTPS proxy URL for sandbox services, with optional public-access restrictions. URLs are public by default; proxy terminates TLS and can re-encrypt to configured HTTPS ports, not TLS passthrough. Adapter configures no service/preview or public-access restriction.

self_hosting.notes: Official open-source runtime/control plane is Apache-2.0. gpu.notes: Official OpenSandbox ResourceLimits schema describes gpu device counts. Requires compatible backend mapping, GPU nodes/device integration/isolation and image; not universal Docker/Firecracker support. AgentRun model-runtime GPU is not managed sandbox GPU evidence; latter unknown.

network_policy.notes: OpenSandbox policy/enforcement deployment-dependent: Docker sidecar requires bridge and config, DNS mode not CIDR enforcement; IPv6 gaps. AgentRun VPC/PrivateLink does not prove upstream per-sandbox egress-schema parity.

persistent_storage.notes: OpenSandbox host/PVC/OSSFS volumes and backend snapshots; pool-mode storage configured in template. AgentRun OSS/NAS documented. Rootfs/session alone not indefinite durable storage.

session_reuse.notes: OpenSandbox sandbox ID/lifecycle renew and backend-specific pause/resume; AgentRun file/session management. Rootfs snapshot not generic memory checkpoint; no repo multiturn run.

shell.notes: OpenSandbox commands.run shell documented. Managed AgentRun chosen image/tool/API governs shell availability; no blanket upstream interface inheritance.

file_transfer.notes: OpenSandbox file SDK/API and managed AgentRun file management documented; exact managed file transport limits unverified.

ports_preview.notes: OpenSandbox port endpoint with configured ingress/proxy. Managed Browser CDP/WebSocket specific to browser; not general public preview guarantee.

self_hosting.notes: OpenSandbox self-hostable on Docker/Kubernetes, including configured isolation profiles; managed AgentRun backend not thereby self-hostable.

cmek.notes: No native sandbox CMEK API or managed AgentRun sandbox key coverage verified. Infrastructure/storage encryption choices are distinct.

k8s_agent_sandbox.name: Kubernetes adapter
k8s_agent_sandbox.customization_summary: Deployment unattested. Adapter talks HTTP to an existing AGENT_SANDBOX_URL or, by default, auto-spawns the repository FastAPI/uvicorn server as a host subprocess. That fallback is not Kubernetes-SIGs controller/CRD provisioning or managed GKE isolation. Official Kubernetes deployments allow image/resource/storage/network configuration; GKE offers a managed controller add-on on an operator-configured cluster. Saved results must not be assigned a security ranking.

custom_image.notes: Official Sandbox/SandboxTemplate podTemplate selects a container image. Adapter sends no image and does not create templates/claims; auto_spawn uses host Python. Repository YAML/image is deployment intent, not evidence that it ran.

runtime_packages.notes: A chosen image can bundle dependencies and runtime installation depends on permission/egress. Saved report observes preinstalled packages and pip availability, not installing a new package. Auto-spawn inherits the host runtime and network.

cpu_sizing.notes: Official pod templates support requests/limits. Repository manifest requests 500m and limits 2 CPUs; adapter sends neither and auto-spawn sets no CPU constraint. Report's cost assumption of 2 vCPU does not attest effective allocation.

memory_sizing.notes: Official pod templates support memory requests/limits. Repository manifest requests 1Gi and limits 4Gi; adapter sends neither. Saved allocation workload reaching 2000MB is not a 4Gi limit or allocation measurement. Actual deployment limits unknown.

gpu.notes: A real GKE gVisor deployment can use supported GPUs for CUDA under version/model/driver constraints; microVM sandbox runtimes do not support GPUs per reviewed GKE docs. Adapter/manifest request no accelerator and report contains no GPU inventory. No accelerator access is attested here.

network_policy.notes: Official GKE add-on manages ingress/egress policies and permits template customization. Auto-spawn installs no network policy. Report observed DNS/HTTP allowed and metadata URL failure, which does not prove an enforced isolation policy or identify the deployment.

persistent_storage.notes: Upstream supports persistent storage surviving Pod restarts when configured. Local fallback uses a shared temporary base directory removed in teardown; per-run cleanup is a no-op. No PVC/mount/retention attestation in report or local template.

session_reuse.notes: Upstream provides stable stateful Sandbox identity/lifecycle. This adapter targets one HTTP server/base directory with no claim/session allocation. A five-turn loop inside one execution does not prove independently isolated cross-request sessions.

shell.notes: Saved Python workloads ran through /execute. Repository server executes arbitrary commands with asyncio.create_subprocess_shell in a working directory; auto-spawn imposes no kernel/container boundary. Measured command execution is not measured sandbox isolation.

file_transfer.notes: HTTP upload/download are implemented, but the saved roundtrip stdout says 20 output bytes with SHA 03f8b5a6985317bb443711cf59982832808ed02a2a2b2c2e7c07bd702ac081e9 while collected artifact is 35 bytes with SHA 1093d1f916b518786a39c26266690572a4dfb9b7273ca21cf923acd9e42fa394. This is not a verified byte-faithful roundtrip. Adapter collects only two candidate paths.

ports_preview.notes: Official deployments route HTTP through a Sandbox Router and production direct/Gateway connections. Operator configures services, exposure and authentication; no automatic public preview URL. Local port 8888 is an execution API, not proof of application-port preview support.

self_hosting.notes: Upstream is a Kubernetes CRD/controller installed on an operator cluster; GKE alternatively manages the controller add-on. Adapter can run its local server but does not provision either deployment. The saved deployment remains unattested.

cmek.notes: GKE can use customer-managed keys for node boot disks and attached Persistent Disks/Filestore with explicit KMS/IAM/StorageClass setup. This is infrastructure/storage-specific, not an Agent Sandbox API guarantee; control-plane disks cannot use CMEK. No key configured by adapter or attested in report.

cost_model.model_text: No universal Kubernetes-SIGs per-execution tariff; pay for deployed infrastructure, warm pools, router/controller capacity, storage and networking. GKE Agent Sandbox adds no feature fee; normal GKE pricing applies.
cost_model.limitations: Deployment unattested, so no measured cloud cost. Saved $0.000072/second and 2-vCPU/4-GB inputs have no bill/SKU provenance. Warm pool idle capacity and cluster/router/storage costs cannot be omitted. GKE monthly eligible cluster-fee credit is $74.40 per billing account, not free workload compute. No historical increase or security ranking asserted.

method_notes: No composite capability or confidence score is used. Unknown requirements stay unresolved.
Eligible cohorts require >=5 correctness-validated attempts; five passes still give a 95% Wilson lower bound of only ~56.6%.
Client wall time includes cleanup and is not pure cold provisioning.
Different providers faced different tasks and counts; totals are coverage, not pooled vendor reliability.
Pricing is published list rate, reviewed 2026-10-13, never invoice-backed. GB is not GiB; a physical core is not a vCPU.
Unknown capability is not a no; conditional capability is not a yes. A documented feature is not a tested deployment.
Local control is a measurement baseline, never a secure runtime for untrusted code.
